justification: Headline artefact is ClawArena-Team, a 41-scenario benchmark and SMS score isolating subagent-management ability rather than a coordination mechanism; twelve models scored in the lab, no deployment.

VISO-PC's claim is the independent verifier that accepts only candidates satisfying constraints and yielding a verified rate; evaluated against fixed single-solver baselines on a self-built prototype, not in operation.

FAME contributes orchestration machinery that fixes step execution: modular service composition, checkpointing, suspend and callback resume; measured in the lab over 26 MCP tasks and MLE-Bench MLZero workloads.

ToolSmith's mechanism is the validation gate: generated NL tests executed in a sandbox plus API state confirmation decide whether a tool stands; the abstract argues the framework with no reported evaluation.

Object of study is the reviewer-feedback revision step, with 85-100% of hallucinated blogs rewritten after critique; evidence is 4,900 lab runs over primary/reviewer model combinations on a fictional-artist probe.
Proposes a modular architecture of specialised agents with bounded roles and hand-offs, i.e. the arrangement itself; argued as a Viewpoint and demonstrated only through one clinical scenario design.

Core component is the OVON NLP interface carrying structured JSON assessments between four levels of specialised agents, so the contribution is inter-agent communication; over 300 induced-hallucination prompts run in the lab.

CellPilot's credited mechanism is structured workflow control with observation-guided plan, execute, inspect and revise steps; validated on GTEx, Tabula Sapiens and Mouse Cell Atlas datasets, not in analysis practice.

The agent's contribution is orchestrating sampling, simulation and retraining with dynamic strategy switching that decides the next step, credited with ~6% lower SMAPE against single-strategy runs on simulator prototypes.
Headline artefact is a three-dimension benchmark suite (workflow, RAG gating, HPC) with EngiAI presented as its reference implementation; four LLM backends scored on EngiBench problems in the lab.

Audio-Mind's stated challenge is deciding when agentic evidence acquisition is warranted, preserving the frontend answer otherwise and bounding external evidence; evidence is MMAR and MSU-Bench accuracy.

Two of three contributions are the measuring instrument, Node F1, SSI and Tool F1 plus an AsyncHow-based dataset, and the conclusions are about which metrics predict agent performance; lab analysis with statistical testing.

CoThinker operationalises cognitive load theory as agent specialisation plus structured communication and a collective working memory, i.e. the arrangement; tested on complex tasks against fabricated high-load conditions.

CAAF's central pillar is a Harness of machine-readable domain invariants enforced by a deterministic assertion interface that must pass before output stands; the architectural claim rests on three-tier UAI ablations.

ALAS's credited mechanism is disruption handling by history-aware local compensation instead of global replanning over decomposed plans; results reported on job-shop scheduling benchmarks in static and dynamic settings.

BRACE decides whether to replan and allocates an explicit token budget and latency SLO per call, leaving the planner intact; validated on Meta Habitat, RoboFactory and AirSim with SLO-violation and token measurements.
Contribution is the replanning trigger: interrupt the running skill only when partner actions contradict the inferred one, versus constant replanning; measured on Overcooked benchmarks in simulation.

ToolMaze is the artefact, a perturbation benchmark with DAG complexity and a 2x2 fault taxonomy measuring recovery; the paper scores existing models and reports PRR drops rather than proposing a recovery mechanism.

APB is a diagnostic benchmark of 4,209 cases isolating planning from execution failure, an instrument rather than a planning mechanism; 12 MLLMs plus ToolSandbox and tau^2-bench runs are all lab evaluations.

PDoctor is a diagnostic instrument: it synthesises constraint-derived user inputs as a testing oracle to expose and characterise erroneous plans; evaluated across three agent frameworks and two LLMs in the lab.

DRL-derived parameter knowledge is injected in-context to constrain which adjustment the agent takes next in each iteration, i.e. action selection; guided versus unguided planning compared over prostate and liver cases.

Tensor-Coord formalises the joint plan of N agents as a tensor whose CP rank measures coordination complexity and whose residual localises inter-agent conflicts; tested on 2-, 3- and 4-agent delivery grids.

SERP's stated shift is from frozen to evolving models, upgrading the action model at run time from recent experience via in-context learning with auto-differentiation; simulation and real-world benchmark runs.
Audits one mechanism, the LLM acting as a step-wise action-selection policy that observes each state and can reset, against direct prompting and Fast Downward on 102 IPC Blocksworld instances.

Robotouille is a benchmark environment with synchronous and asynchronous datasets built to measure long-horizon asynchronous planning; the paper scores ReAct (gpt4-o) and analyses failure modes in simulation.
